name: tech.krate/krate
title: Krate
description: Make an app by asking. Krate builds and checks it, and its link opens in any browser, phones too.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Search the public Krate gallery for apps by words. Results are ranked by how well the words match the app's name, then its description and publisher. Each result has the app's link (opens in Krate), a link that opens it in a browser tab, what it is allowed to do in plain words, its size, and whether its publisher is verified and the app signed.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "markdown editor"

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: One public Krate app's details, from its link or id: what it does, what it is allowed to do in plain words, its versions, size, publisher and signature, its link and its browser link. Accepts a hub link (https://hub.krate.tech/a/..., /run/...), the app's own id (v followed by 11 hex characters), a short id, or a full hash. An app removed from the registry answers with its removal notice only.

id_or_link.description: A Krate app link, or its id

tools.name: list_featured
tools.description: The Krate gallery's front shelves: the apps picked to start with, and the newest apps, each with its link, what it is allowed to do in plain words, its size and its publisher.

tools.name: get_krate_guide
tools.description: Krate's reference for writing a Krate app (a native app for Windows, macOS and Linux that also opens in a browser): the files an app is made of (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, manifest.toml), the API it may use, the permissions it may declare, the mistakes that fail a first build, and worked examples. No sign-in needed.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Searches Krate's public apps and Krate's guide to making an app. Each result has an id, a title and a link; the guide's id is krate-guide.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "markdown editor"

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: One Krate app or Krate's guide in full, by the id a result carries: an app's details and permissions in plain words, or the whole guide to making an app.

id.description: A result's id, an app's link, or krate-guide

tools.name: build_app
tools.description: Builds a real app the person keeps: one small file that runs natively on Windows, macOS and Linux and opens from a link in any browser, phones included. A Krate app keeps its own data on the device and works offline; with the person's permission it can print to a printer they pick with no print dialog, talk to serial and USB devices, read and write Excel files, serve other devices on the local network, and use the camera, microphone and location. Compiles the app's files (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, manifest.toml and any assets), checks it uses only Krate's API and runs it once, then publishes it unlisted to the signed-in person's Krate account with its link. Answers a build id at once; a build takes a few minutes. Needs the person to sign in to Krate.

name.description: The app's name, as a person would say it

files.description: Every file of the app, with paths relative to the app folder

content.description: The file's text, or base64 when encoding is base64

encoding.description: base64 for a picture or other binary asset

tools.name: build_status
tools.description: The state of a Krate build, by its build id: still building, failed, or published. A failed build's answer has Krate's check in its own words: the stage, what went wrong and how to fix it. A published build's answer has the app's link and a browser link that opens it on any device, nothing to install. Needs the person to sign in to Krate.

build_id.description: The build id a build answered with
